payload.blocks: Only the shape of the privileged-chores mechanism (p-g5ktat4kej): settled design, task list and the planner hand-off. Clarifying points P1-P6 continue.
payload.headline: Privileged chores for confined heads: one policy door with rules as data, instead of one verb per chore?

parts.cause: Read head-grants.mjs and head-request.mjs: 28 verbs, each a hand-written case. So every new chore means a new door. In the 20:01 session the supervisor already held `config patch` but could not see its own grant, so it asked you. polkit, Kubernetes RBAC, Codex auto-review and Claude Code all use one broker with policy as data, plus a can-i lookup.

options.cost: About 300-450 lines of src plus tests in src/session-host and core/config-standard; 1-2 days.
options.does: One verb `chore <action> <resource>` plus `chore can-i`. A data table holds persona, action, resource kind, a checkable condition and yes or ask-owner. ask-owner parks a five-part question with the exact command. Every call is logged. Supervisor wake runs the recurring rows.
options.gain: A new chore is a table row, never a new verb. Heads see their own rights. You get choices, not commands.
options.harm: One more verb now. A rule-order mistake could over-grant (the known polkit risk), so rows need a test each.
options.label: A. One policy door, rules as data

options.does: Heads write intent into a file they own; a host-side controller makes reality match it (Kubernetes operator, Atlantis).
options.gain: No calls at all for recurring chores; drift heals itself.
options.harm: A one-off chore must be phrased as state, and each resource kind still needs its own reconcile code, so code grows per kind.
options.label: B. Desired-state reconciler

options.does: Bring back one unconfined session that does every privileged chore.
options.gain: Works today with almost no code.
options.harm: Reverses your 2026-11-21 decision to retire it, and removes confinement from the longest-running head.
options.label: C. Standing unconfined lead:SUPERVISOR

options.harm: The door count keeps growing, which is exactly what you asked to stop.
options.label: D. Keep adding one verb per chore

parts.recommendation: A. It is what polkit, Kubernetes RBAC and Codex auto-review do. It stops door growth at the root, fixes the can-i gap that caused 20:01, and keeps confinement. B's recurring-cleanup gain is kept by letting the supervisor wake call A's recurring rows.

scope.allows: Settling the shape as A and writing the design, task list and planner hand-off in DISCUSSION.md. Whether the 28 existing verbs move into the table is asked separately.
scope.forbids: Any code, plan or backlog change by this shaper, and folding the existing 28 verbs into A without a separate decision.

parts.what: Since the manual lead:SUPERVISOR stopped, the confined supervisor sends routine chores to you: raise maxLeads, remove landed worktrees. You asked for no more narrow doors, one per chore, and for the shape to follow what the world does.
